GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2015-10-22T13:31:12Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: SwitchMap with connectable's Replay raise exception
Description: For the following code:

``` java
ConnectableObservable<Long> replayObs = Observable.interval(3, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
        .startWith(-5L)
        .switchMap(aLong -> {
            if (aLong == 2L) {
                return Observable.error(new NullPointerException());
            } else {
                return Observable.just(aLong);
            }
        })
        .replay(1);

replayObs.connect(Actions.empty());

replayObs
        .subscribe(s -> {
            Log.wtf("MainActivity ", "call " + s);
        }, throwable -> {
            Log.wtf("MainActivity ", throwable);
        });
```

It emmits the following:

```
MainActivity: call -5
MainActivity: java.lang.IllegalStateException: more items arrived than were requested
MainActivity:     at rx.internal.producers.ProducerArbiter.produced(ProducerArbiter.java:98)
```

I realize that the `.connect` is happening before the first `.subscribe` but if I have `.flatpMap` instead, which has a different producer, it doesn't complain.

This is the simplest way to raise the exception:

``` java
ConnectableObservable<Long> replayObs = Observable.just(1l)
        .switchMap(Observable::just)
    //  .onBackpressureBuffer(1)
        .replay(1);
```

Adding a onBackpreassureBuffer(1) before the .replay() solves the problem. Is that a correct solution? Is that a bug in the `ProducerArbiter`?

llm_response:
CATEGORY: 2
REASONING: This issue involves a specific bug in RxJava's operator behavior when using switchMap with connectable's Replay. To verify the solution (adding onBackpressureBuffer(1) before replay()), one would need to run the code and confirm that the IllegalStateException no longer occurs. This requires setting up a build environment with RxJava dependencies to execute the code and observe the behavior. The issue is purely related to software behavior and doesn't involve any special hardware, network dependencies, or platform-specific requirements. It can be easily containerized in a Docker environment with Java and the appropriate RxJava libraries installed, making it straightforward to reproduce and verify the solution.
